title: Birbal and the Astrologer
summary: A fraudulent astrologer predicts that Akbar will die if he leaves the palace on a Tuesday. Birbal reveals the astrologer's ignorance with an unexpected question.
full_text:
A traveling astrologer named Pandit Dinanath arrived in Agra, adorned with astrological charts, brass sundials, and mystical stones. Claiming to read the celestial movements of the stars with infallible precision, he gained an audience with Emperor Akbar.

After calculating Akbar's horoscope with dramatic sighs, the astrologer whispered in terror: 'O Emperor! The malefic planet Saturn has aligned with Mars! A catastrophic doom hangs over your head! If Your Majesty sets foot outside the palace gates next Tuesday, the angel of death shall strike you down before sunset!'

Akbar, deeply disturbed by the prophecy, canceled state tours and ordered the palace gates barred. The entire administration was paralyzed by superstition.

Birbal arrived at court on Monday morning and found Akbar sitting in gloom. Learning of the prophecy, Birbal asked to interview the famed astrologer.

Pandit Dinanath arrived, chanting mantras and boasting: 'My charts never fail, Raja Birbal! The stars have written the Emperor's destiny in stone!'

Birbal smiled politely: 'Panditji, your knowledge of celestial constellations is astonishing. Tell me—can your charts also foresee the future of ordinary mortals?'

'Of course!' the astrologer boasted. 'I know the exact day, hour, and minute when every man in this room shall depart from this earth!'

Birbal leaned forward, his eyes sharp: 'Then tell me, wise astrologer: can you tell this court the exact day and hour of your own death?'

The astrologer puffed his chest: 'Certainly! The stars have decreed that I shall live to the ripe old age of ninety-five, dying peacefully in my bed surrounded by grandchildren!'

The instant the words left the astrologer's lips, Birbal drew his sharp dagger from his waist, held the blade directly before the astrologer's throat, and said to Emperor Akbar:

'Sire! Give me the command, and I shall sever this fraud's neck right now, proving that he cannot foresee his own death even sixty seconds into the future!'

The astrologer let out a shriek of terror, dropped his charts, threw himself at Akbar's feet, and confessed:

'Mercy! Mercy, Lord Birbal! I know nothing of the future! I invented the prophecy to terrify the Emperor so that he would pay me five thousand gold coins for expensive protective rituals!'

Akbar was furious at the deception, but laughed at how Birbal had shattered the charlatan's web with a single question. Akbar banished the astrologer, rode through the city on Tuesday in glorious health, and thanked Birbal for liberating his mind from fear.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
